title: Metro line linking airport and old town opens
summary: Riverton's long-awaited Metro line connecting the airport to the old town opened to commuters on Monday. Officials expect 80,000 daily riders, with trains every six minutes at peak hours. Tickets can be bought through a new mobile app or at station kiosks.

title: Village school wins award for solar classrooms
summary: A government school in Ashgrove has won a national award after moving its classrooms to rooftop solar power. Students run a weekly energy audit, and savings on bills have paid for a new library and a science kit for every grade.

title: Farmers adopt phone-based weather alerts
summary: Thousands of farmers in the Kaveri belt now receive free rainfall and frost alerts by text message in their own language. Early users say the warnings helped them delay sowing twice this season and saved roughly a fifth of their seed.

title: Pre-monsoon showers bring relief after heatwave
summary: Cities across the central plains recorded their first pre-monsoon showers overnight, bringing temperatures down by five degrees after a week-long heatwave. Forecasters say more scattered rain is likely through the weekend, though they urge residents to keep drinking plenty of water.

title: Nations agree on shared rules for ocean plastic
summary: Delegates from forty countries signed an agreement to cut single-use plastic dumped into the sea by half before 2035. Wealthier nations promised funding for waste collection in coastal towns, while fishing fleets must now report any lost nets within a day.

title: Coastal city tests floating gardens against floods
summary: Planners in Port Elmsworth have anchored a dozen floating gardens along the harbour to soak up storm surges and shelter wildlife. If the six-month trial reduces flooding in nearby streets, the city plans to build forty more along its waterfront.

title: Peace talks resume after a three-month pause
summary: Delegates from two neighbouring countries returned to the negotiating table on Thursday after a three-month break. Mediators described the opening session as constructive and said discussions will focus on trade routes and shared river water before any wider agreement is attempted.

title: Historic library reopens after decade of restoration
summary: The Grand Harbour Library welcomed visitors again this weekend after ten years of restoration. Its painted ceiling, rare map room and original reading desks have been carefully repaired, and entry is free for students during the first month.

title: Local startup raises funds to recycle old batteries
summary: Voltloop, a three-year-old startup, has raised funding to expand its plant that recovers lithium and cobalt from old phone and laptop batteries. The company says it can recycle ninety percent of material and plans to open collection points in twelve cities.

title: Retail sales rise as festive shopping begins early
summary: Retailers reported a twelve percent jump in weekend sales as shoppers started festive purchases earlier than usual. Clothing and home appliances led the rise, while analysts note that online discounts and easier instalment plans are encouraging customers to spend sooner.

title: Coffee prices dip after record harvest
summary: Wholesale coffee prices fell to a two-year low after growers reported their largest harvest on record. Cafe owners say they will keep menu prices steady for now, while farmers worry that lower returns could make it harder to cover rising labour costs.

title: Open-source browser adds built-in reading mode
summary: A popular open-source web browser has added a reading mode that strips adverts and sidebars from articles and lets users change font size and spacing. Developers say the feature runs entirely on the device, so no browsing data is sent anywhere.

title: New budget phone promises three-day battery life
summary: A new budget smartphone launched this week claims to last three days on a single charge, thanks to a larger battery and a low-power display. Reviewers praise its endurance but say the camera struggles in dim light and storage cannot be expanded.

title: Students build low-cost robot to sort waste
summary: A team of engineering students has built a robot that sorts paper, plastic and metal waste using a simple camera and a small motor arm. It costs under ten thousand rupees, and a local housing society will test it next month.

title: Quantum-safe messaging app enters public beta
summary: A new messaging app that uses encryption designed to resist future quantum computers has opened its public beta. Security researchers will review its code over the coming weeks, and the makers say messages will remain private even from the company itself.

title: Astronomers spot faint comet visible this week
summary: Astronomers have found a faint comet that should be visible through binoculars in the pre-dawn sky this week. It will be closest to Earth on Friday, and observers are advised to look low in the east away from city lights.

title: Deep-sea survey finds dozens of unknown species
summary: A month-long deep-sea survey has recorded more than forty species new to science, including a transparent squid and a worm that glows blue. Researchers say the creatures live near hot vents and could reveal how life copes with extreme pressure.

title: Researchers grow crops in simulated Mars soil
summary: Scientists have grown tomatoes and spinach in soil designed to mimic the surface of Mars, using treated waste water and a mix of friendly bacteria. The harvest was small but safe to eat, giving hope for future long-distance space missions.

title: Underdogs clinch league title on last-day goal
summary: Lakeside United won their first league title in thirty years after a stoppage-time goal sealed a two-one victory on the final day. Thousands of fans poured onto the pitch, and the club captain dedicated the win to the volunteers who kept the team alive.

title: Teen sprinter breaks 15-year-old state record
summary: Seventeen-year-old sprinter Meera Das broke the state 100-metre record on Sunday, finishing in 11.42 seconds and beating a mark that had stood for fifteen years. Her coach says she now plans to compete at the national junior championships next month.

title: Cricket academy opens free coaching for girls
summary: A new cricket academy in Kalyanpur has opened free coaching for girls aged ten to sixteen, with kits and travel costs covered by local sponsors. More than two hundred players signed up on the first day, filling every batch until the end of the year.

title: Indie film about a lighthouse keeper tops festival
summary: A quiet independent film about a lighthouse keeper and his stubborn parrot took the top prize at this year's coastal film festival. Jurors praised its patient storytelling and stunning sea photography, and the film will reach cinemas next month.

title: Beloved radio drama returns for a new season
summary: The family radio drama Evening Lane is returning for a new season after a two-year break. Original cast members will voice their characters again, and the first episode, set during a village fair, will air on Sunday at eight.

title: Street musicians get a weekend stage downtown
summary: The city council has set aside a permanent weekend stage downtown for street musicians, with free sound equipment and a simple booking system. Performers say the move will help them earn steady tips without worrying about complaints or sudden removals.

title: City council approves free bus passes for students
summary: Riverton's city council voted on Tuesday to give free bus passes to all school and college students from next term. Supporters say it will cut traffic near campuses, while opponents want a clearer plan for paying the estimated yearly cost.

title: Voters to choose new ward representatives next month
summary: Election officials announced that residents of twelve wards will vote next month to choose new representatives. Polling stations will open earlier this year, and first-time voters can register online until the end of the week using a simple form.

title: Youth forum debates shorter school hours
summary: Teenagers from across the region held a mock assembly on Saturday to debate shorter school hours and longer sports periods. Organisers said the best proposals will go to the education board, which has promised to read every submission.

title: Free eye check-up camps reach rural districts
summary: Mobile clinics have begun offering free eye tests in remote villages, screening more than five thousand people in the first fortnight. Volunteers say many patients had never visited an eye doctor, and free spectacles will be delivered within two weeks.

title: Study links daily walking to better sleep
summary: A year-long study of three thousand adults found that people who walked briskly for thirty minutes a day fell asleep faster and woke less often at night. Researchers say the benefit appeared within a month, and no special equipment was needed.

title: Hospital launches pocket guide for first-time parents
summary: A city hospital has released a free pocket guide that explains newborn feeding, sleep and vaccination schedules in simple language. Nurses will hand copies to every new family, and an audio version in four languages is planned for next month.
